advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop test_generator_source_has_no_intercept_regex (source-grep of the module under test); its AC2 intent is already covered behaviorally by test_no_curated_census_symbols_remain's hasattr assertions.
evidence: tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py:129-131: `assert "INTERCEPT_COMMANDS" not in source` / `assert "ladder_intercepts" not in source` / `assert "argv[0]" not in source`

tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py:119-123: the behavioral equivalent already covers AC2 via module attributes: `assert not hasattr(gen, "INTERCEPT_COMMANDS")` / `assert not hasattr(gen, "ladder_intercepts")`

GEN_PATH is the source under test (tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py:28: `GEN_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "gen_cli_reference.py"`), so grepping its text is source-grepping, not a structural-artifact grep on an instruction file.
advisory.finding: test_generator_source_has_no_intercept_regex greps the source text of the module under test (scripts/gen_cli_reference.py) rather than its behavior: it asserts the literal substrings 'INTERCEPT_COMMANDS', 'ladder_intercepts', and 'argv[0]' are absent from GEN_PATH.read_text(). This is a source-grepping / change-detector test that breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (a renamed internal, or the token appearing in a comment/docstring), and 'argv[0]' in particular maps to no observable contract. The behavioral equivalent already exists (test_no_curated_census_symbols_remain asserts `not hasattr(gen, ...)`).
advisory.suggested_fix: Delete test_generator_source_has_no_intercept_regex and rely on test_no_curated_census_symbols_remain (hasattr checks) for the AC2 'census is deleted' contract; if a stronger guarantee is wanted, assert the generator's observable output/derivation rather than its source text.

coaching.subject: masked rebar-mcp exit code in smoke-test pipeline

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the generator's help-backed/intercept split with the registry's authoritative `Route.intercept` flag so `metrics`/`audit` (intercept=True, group=static_read) are classified consistently.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:430-445 `metrics` and `audit` are declared with `group="static_read"` and `intercept=True`
src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:590 `_INTERCEPTS` is derived as `frozenset(r.name for r in live if r.intercept)` — the authoritative intercept set uses `r.intercept`, not `group`

EDITORIAL_PREAMBLE (scripts/gen_cli_reference.py:51-52) asserts 'intercept-arm commands ... each owns its own `--help`, rendered live from its parser here.' — but metrics/audit render from pinned bytes
dropped.finding: The generator classifies help-backed vs intercept rendering by `route.group != "intercept"`, but the registry's authoritative intercept marker is the boolean `Route.intercept`. `metrics` and `audit` are `intercept=True` with `group="static_read"`, so they are rendered from committed help bytes (help-backed path) instead of live from their parser — contradicting the registry's own intercept classification and the preamble's claim that intercept-arm commands 'render live from their parser'.
dropped.suggested_fix: In `_syntax_body`, branch on `route.intercept` (the authoritative marker) rather than `route.group != "intercept"`, or explicitly document/justify why group is used and add a drift check that the two predicates agree.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `set -o pipefail` (or capture and assert rebar-mcp's exit code) so the `rebar-mcp --help | grep` smoke-test fails when the entry point exits non-zero.
evidence: No `set -o pipefail` appears in this step (the per-extra loop step); the run block relies on `bash -e` errexit only (see comment lines 222-226 describing errexit/&&-chain behavior).
Commit message intent: 'smoke-tests the separate rebar-mcp entry point on a concrete --help observable' — a masked non-zero exit undermines that observable.
dropped.finding: The rebar-mcp smoke-test pipes `--help` into `grep -q` without `set -o pipefail`, so a non-zero exit from the `rebar-mcp` entry point is masked by grep; the check only asserts the string 'rebar-mcp' appears somewhere in output, not that the entry point exited cleanly.
scenarios: `rebar-mcp --help` starts to exit non-zero (e.g. broken lazy import) but its argparse usage/stdout still contains the literal 'rebar-mcp' — grep succeeds and the mcp extra lane passes green.
dropped.suggested_fix: Prepend `set -o pipefail` to the step's run block, or restructure as `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp" --help >"$RUNNER_TEMP/mcp_help" && grep -q "rebar-mcp" "$RUNNER_TEMP/mcp_help"` so a non-zero exit from rebar-mcp fails the check.
